transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess what brings me in is I just don’t have the push like I used to. I used to go to choir, and I had my quilting, and I’d visit folks, you know—there was one lady from church, she always liked when I brought those little squares, the blue ones were her favorite—anyway, now most days I just sit at home with the TV on low. I know people are expecting me sometimes, and I just… don’t get myself up to go.
How long have you been feeling this way, without much motivation or interest in doing things you used to enjoy?

It’s been… well, I’d say it started after I retired from the school office. That was a little over two years ago now. I used to keep track of all the little papers and attendance slips—funny how busy that kept me—but since then it’s just kind of been building, little by little.
Do you find yourself feeling down or hopeless most days, or feeling like you're not worth much?

I don’t know that I’d call it hopeless, exactly. I mean, some mornings are heavier than others, and I look around at the dishes or the sewing basket and think, “Well, that’s just sitting there again.” But then I get thinking about how my mother used to keep all her thread in old cookie tins—those blue Danish ones, you know—and I still have one somewhere.

As far as not being worth much… I don’t really sit and say that to myself, no. It’s more like I just don’t get moving. I’m not sure if that’s the same thing you mean.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep or appetite lately, or do you often find yourself feeling guilty about things?

Sleep and eating… I don’t know, I haven’t really kept track. Some nights I’m up looking at the ceiling, but then I remember I forgot to put the porch light on, and then I get thinking about when my husband used to say that light brought every moth in the county.

Appetite, well… I eat what’s there, I suppose. Nothing special to say. And guilty… I’m not sure. I don’t sit around naming it that. Maybe I feel bad when I miss something I meant to do, but guilty sounds like a bigger word than what I’d use.
Do you find yourself feeling down or sad most days, even if it's not necessarily hopeless or overwhelming?

Sad most days… I don’t know if I’d say it like that. Some days I’m just sitting there and the house feels too quiet, but then I’ll notice the curtains need washing, or I’ll think about that little grocery on Maple that used to have the good peaches—oh, they were so much better than what they sell now.

So… I’m not sure. I don’t really keep count of “most days.” It’s more like I get slowed down, if that makes sense.
Would you say that most days you feel down or sad, even if it's not extremely intense?

I’m not really sure how to answer “most days.” I don’t sit there thinking, “I’m sad now,” you know? Some days I feel kind of low or slow, but then I get looking at the dust on the windowsill, and I remember my aunt used to say if you could write your name in it, it was time to clean.

So… maybe sometimes. I wouldn’t know if it’s most days. It’s not something I’ve been counting.
Would you say that, when you’re feeling slowed down or low, it’s often accompanied by a feeling of sadness or emptiness, even if it doesn’t feel overwhelming?

I don’t know if I’d call it emptiness. That sounds like a big hollow room or something. Sometimes I’m just… not moving much, kind of sitting there, and then I’ll notice the clock ticking too loud. My mother had a clock like that in the kitchen, always ran a little fast.

So maybe it’s sad, maybe it’s just being tired in my head. I can’t really tell the difference sometimes.
Do you often feel like you don’t have any energy, or that even small tasks take a lot out of you?

Yes… I think that’s part of it. I just don’t have the push I used to. Like choir—I used to get myself dressed and go, and quilting too, and visiting people. Now even thinking about getting ready feels like a lot.

Most days I just sit at home with the TV on low. Not even really watching it. And I know folks are expecting me sometimes, or maybe wondering where I am, but I just… don’t get up and go. The other day I thought about calling someone, and then I saw a thread on my sleeve and started picking at it instead. So yes, small things do take a lot out of me, I guess.
Would you say that most days you feel down or sad, even if it’s just a little or not overwhelming?

I’m not sure I’d say sad most days. It’s more like… I get quiet and slow, and then I forget what I was going to do. Sometimes there’s a heaviness, but I don’t know if that’s sadness or just being worn down.

My neighbor used to say you can tell a person’s mood by whether their curtains are open, but mine are half-open a lot because the rod sticks on one side. So… I don’t know. Maybe a little sometimes, but I can’t say for sure it’s most days.
When you think about the things you used to enjoy, like choir, quilting, or visiting people, do you still get any pleasure or satisfaction from them, even if you don’t end up doing them?

I suppose… if I think about choir, I can remember liking it, the way the voices all came together. And quilting, I used to feel good seeing the little squares line up right.

But now it’s like there’s no push in me to get there, or even to start. Visiting folks too—I know people might be expecting me, and I used to enjoy that, sitting and talking a while. These days I mostly just stay home with the TV on low, and sometimes it’s not even a program I care about. It’s just on.

So I don’t know if I get much pleasure from thinking about those things now. Mostly I just think, “I should go,” and then I don’t.
Would you say that, overall, your mood has been down or low more days than not in the past few weeks?

More days than not… I don’t know how to count it, really. Some mornings I’m just slow getting up, but I wouldn’t always call it low. It’s like when the kettle sits there and you forget you put the water on—well, mine’s electric now, my daughter said it’s safer.

I guess there are days I feel kind of heavy, but other days I’m just sitting there, not much of anything. So I’m not sure I can say it’s been down more days than not. It’s hard for me to tell.
When you think about the things you used to enjoy, like choir or quilting, do you still feel any joy or interest in them, even if you aren't doing them now?

I used to, I think. Choir especially… there was something nice about everybody’s voices, and quilting kept my hands busy. But now when I think of them, it’s more like I know I ought to want to go, but I don’t feel that push.

Most days I just end up at home, TV on low. Sometimes I know folks are expecting me, or I think maybe I should visit, and then I just… don’t. It’s not that I hate those things. The interest just doesn’t seem to carry me there anymore.
Would you say that most days, even if not all the time, you feel down, sad, or low in mood?

I’m not real sure. Some days I feel kind of… flat, I guess, but I don’t always know if that’s sad. My daughter asks me that too sometimes, and then I start thinking about whether I slept right or if I ate, and then I forget what I was answering.

So, most days? I can’t say for sure. I haven’t noticed it like that, like crying or saying “I’m sad” every day. It’s more just sitting there and the day goes by.
Would you say that on most days, you feel a persistent sadness or low mood, even if it's not severe?

I don’t know if I’d call it persistent sadness. That sounds more… steady, like a rain that doesn’t stop. Mine isn’t always like that. Sometimes I’m just quiet, or I’m sitting and the TV’s talking more than I am.

Low, maybe some days. But most days? I get mixed up trying to say. Yesterday I meant to fold towels and then I found an old church bulletin in the drawer, and I was thinking about who used to sit in the third pew… so I don’t always keep track of my mood like that. I can’t say for sure.
Would you say that, on most days, you feel a low or sad mood, even if it’s not very strong or overwhelming?

I’m trying to think how to say it right. I don’t wake up and say, “I’m sad,” not most days like that. Sometimes I’m just sort of there, you know, and the house is quiet except the television.

But then I’ll start thinking about whether I fed the cat—well, I don’t have a cat now, but we had one years ago—and then my mind goes off. So I don’t know if that counts as low mood. I haven’t really noticed it in a clear way.
Would you say that on most days, you feel a low or sad mood, even if it’s not very strong or overwhelming?

I know you asked me that already, and I’m trying not to go in circles. I just… I don’t really have a clear answer. Some days feel kind of dull, like the morning just turns into afternoon, but I don’t know if that means sad.

I used to know the days by when the mailman came, because he’d come right after that game show—well, the old one, not the new host—and now I don’t pay attention the same. So, most days low? I’m not sure. I haven’t noticed it that plain.
Would you say that on most days, you feel a low or sad mood, even if it’s not very strong or overwhelming?

I’m sorry, I know I’m not giving you a straight yes or no. I just don’t really know. Some days I feel kind of flat, or quiet, but I don’t sit there thinking, “this is sadness.”

It’s like when you leave tea too long and it’s not bad, just not right anymore… my mother used to do that, leave the cup by the window. Anyway, I haven’t noticed it being most days in a way I could say for sure.
Would you say that, on most days, you feel a low or sad mood, even if it’s not very strong or overwhelming?

I wish I could give you a clean answer. I just don’t really keep track of it that way. Some mornings are kind of slow, and I sit there a while before I do anything, but I don’t know if that’s being sad or just… the day being quiet.

My sister used to say I always looked serious, even when I was just listening, so maybe people see it different than I feel it. But on most days, low mood… I’m not sure. I haven’t noticed it enough to say yes.
Would you say that on most days, you feel a low or sad mood, even if it’s not very strong or overwhelming?

I hear what you’re asking. I just… I don’t know that I can call it sad most days. Sometimes I’m sitting there and everything feels a little plain, like the color’s washed out, but then the phone rings or I remember I left something in the kitchen and I’m thinking about that instead.

My neighbor used to say mornings tell you what kind of day it’ll be, but I don’t know if that’s true. Some mornings I don’t feel much of anything. So… I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed a low mood every day like that.
Would you say that on most days, you feel a low or sad mood, even if it’s not very strong or overwhelming?

I know you’ve asked it a few times, I’m just having trouble pinning it down. “Low” could mean a lot of things, couldn’t it? Like when the house is too quiet after the television’s been off for a while.

I don’t wake up thinking, oh, I’m sad again. Some days I just move slower, or I sit and look out the window, but then I’ll remember the mail or the kettle, and it changes. So… most days? I don’t think I can say that for sure. I haven’t really noticed it that clearly.
